A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sequential LLM-detection study. Their main text, algorithms, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–I are available and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V2 reports original detection experiments on Olympic news and three text domains, including parameter-estimation and mixed-source studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experimental outcomes in Section 4 and Appendices G–I.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 3 retain the score differences, ONS updates, wealth processes and stopping rules. Algorithm 2's corrected projection index agrees with the projection onto K_{t+1} already specified in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use Olympic news, XSum, WritingPrompts and PubMedQA, with the same source models and domain combinations. The mixed-LLM and mixed human/LLM scenarios already appear in v2.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain the uncorrected and significance-corrected permutation tests. Newly cited Binoculars, ReMoDetect and Raidar do not participate in the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes the reported betting interval from [-1/(2dt), 1/(2dt)] to [-1/(2dt), 0], resolving its inconsistency with the existing composite-test algorithm. This is a reported-setting correction; the PDFs do not establish an experimental rerun.

E4.justification: The score-gap analyses, domain comparisons, 10-versus-20-sample calibration study and mixed-source experiments are retained with the same evidence. No new ablation or robustness study is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 1,000 repeated runs and retain 2,000 permutations per permutation test. No new seed information, confidence intervals or uncertainty-reporting procedure appears.

E6.justification: Numerical table entries and experimental plots are unchanged. Section 4 narrows the Scenario 2 finding that eight Neo-2.7-based score functions control error and detect around t = 300 to a statement about most such functions.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–2 and Appendices D–F are substantially revised. Proposition 1 replaces the d_*^3/Δ^2 bound with logarithmic factors by O((d_*^2/Δ^2) ln(d_*/(αΔ)) + d_*^4/Δ^4), with an analogous composite-test revision. A log-wealth lemma and concentration-based proofs replace the earlier sample-moment wealth analysis.

C1.justification: The conclusion narrows its empirical generalization from most existing detectors to most of the existing detectors the authors use. The central contributions concerning sequential detection, false-positive control and asymptotic power remain.

C2.justification: The introduction adds a concrete explanation of false-positive accumulation under naive sequential reuse of an offline detector, yielding 1−δ^T. The conclusion adds optimistic interior-point betting as a specific future improvement direction.

D1.justification: Appendix I explicitly specifies 20 calibration samples from each sequence. Table 6 clarifies first versus previous samples and removes malformed sample indices. These refine documentation of existing experiments; the generation prompt, core parameter recipes and code/data access remain.

R1.justification: V3 adds references for Binoculars, ReMoDetect, Raidar, Dai et al. (2025) and Chen and Wang (2025), while removing Harvey (2023). Appendix E changes its proof attribution from modifying Chugg et al. to adapting ideas from Dai et al., explaining the different testing settings.

P1.justification: The proof exposition in Appendices D–F is extensively rewritten, including reframing Appendix D around log-wealth and organizing Appendix F into separate validity, power and stopping-time arguments. Introductory motivation is expanded, alongside terminology, title and caption editing.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn with an explicitly labeled Observe stage and revised styling. Captions and placements of algorithms, figures and tables change, while all experimental plots and the existing figure/table inventory are retained.

improvement.justification: V3 improves motivation, qualifies empirical generality and clarifies Figure 1, but the central proof replacement leaves mathematical reliability unresolved. V2's composite proof permits a positive benchmark despite its nonpositive betting domain; v3's Appendix F instead assigns positive growth to both one-sided tests, although only one directional alternative can hold. These different proof gaps prevent a reliable judgment of the revision's net effect on overall quality.
